head: RadPad notebook app turns your notes into a 90s binder
dek: RadPad is a new $1.99 iPhone and iPad notes app made to look like a 1990s school binder, with a randomly printed cover and loose-leaf pages. It was #51 among paid Productivity apps on the US App Store on 17 November.
details: Each copy gets its own cover pattern, such as Memphis squiggles, animal print or neon grids, and you get three re-rolls. Pages curl when you turn them and deleted pages go to a trash you can restore from. It needs no account, has no ads or tracking, and syncs through your own iCloud. Version 1.1 on 17 November added taping photos into the binder; it's made by Safe House Studio LLC and needs iOS 27.
where: iPhone and iPad, iOS 27 or later, $1.99 on the App Store
means: If you like a notes app with some fun to it, RadPad is a one-time $1.99 with no subscription listed and no account.
todo: Find RadPad - 90s Notebook on the App Store; it works on any iPhone with iOS 27, and on an iPhone Duo folding the phone closes the binder.
